correctness.rationale: For a>=4, m=3*2^a and j=2,...,a-2, k=2^j, decompose units by CRT as (C2 x C2^(a-2)) x C2. The first factor has exactly two cyclic order-k subgroups K0,K1, with explicit Q/k-step representatives; each has exactly two graph lifts through the mod-3 sign. For each of the four lifts, least representatives are x+2^a r(x), and r(x) is an explicit periodic mod-3 residue sequence; summing period-3/6 blocks gives the four deficits, for a+j even {P,3P-k,3P,5P-k}, and odd {P-k,3P-k,3P,5P}, P=2^(a-1). All distinct and positive since k<=P/2. The order-two subgroup case is separately counted by eight square roots of 1 (including identity) and D({1,h})=m-1-h; the identity subgroup has deficit m/2-1. Therefore {1,m-1} is uniquely centered among all cyclic subgroups. This uses each subgroup element exactly once, no coset-average substitution; full finite enumeration supports but does not replace CRT and residue summation.
